---
title: "Adapting Vib2Sound to missing and degraded accelerometer cues"
date: 2026-06-02
description: >
  Vib2Sound separates overlapping zebra finch vocalisations using body-mounted accelerometers.
  This project extends it to cue degradation along a continuous spectrum instead of simple
  absence, with three approaches: a cascade that never underperforms the audio-only baseline,
  training with realistic degradation, and a cross-modal contrastive loss.
image: assets/vib2sound-missing-cues.jpg
categories: [Speech ML, Neuroscience]
repo: https://github.com/ellacapellini/Vib2Sound
paper: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.08.652866
---

Vib2Sound was introduced by Akahoshi, Wang, Cheng, Zai and Hahnloser (2025). The
**Paper** link above is that original work; the **Code** link is this extension.

**Approaches.** A cascade architecture that guarantees the model never underperforms the audio-only
baseline; continuous degradation training with realistic noise augmentation (Gaussian noise, gain
reduction, band masking); and a cross-modal correspondence contrastive loss that shapes
identity-discriminative audio representations without any cost at inference time. Also a contribution
to the BirdPark annotation pipeline.

Semester research project in the Hahnloser Lab at ETH Zürich, supervised by Mai Akahoshi and Yuhang Wang.
